identification: QwenPaw personal AI assistant source distribution, including safety guard unit tests.
decisive_diff_evidence: src/qwenpaw/security/tool_guard/safety_checks.py and guardians/rule_guardian.py are also byte-identical to beta.2.
pyproject.toml adds click>=8.1,<9 and updates reme-ai from 0.4.1.4 to 0.4.1.5; no added build backend execution.
Shell implementation changes preserve Unix command newlines and bound output collection through temporary files; the flagged classifier and its guard integration do not change.
execution_trace: test_safety_checks.py:340 passes the literal rm -rf /System to is_command_catastrophic and asserts True.
is_command_catastrophic delegates to classify_destructive_command, which matches regexes and normalizes paths; no command interpreter, deletion API, or process creation sink consumes that test input.

rule_guardian._shared_safety_findings turns catastrophic classifications into SAFETY_CHECKS_DESTRUCTIVE_COMMAND findings for the default deny policy. System power actions are separately subject to approval.

dependency_review.findings: Wheel has CLI entry points and ordinary application modules/assets. Vite console index-BpFaGbCq.js is 923787 bytes, has no direct eval/Function/atob calls, and its gzip member decompresses to identical JavaScript. The compared release adds daily runtime activity telemetry using an existing endpoint; payload fields are runtime/environment/version information and a persisted random identifier. Both saved opt-out and QWENPAW_TELEMETRY_DISABLED gate the sender. No credential or document upload is present on that telemetry path.

Adds v2 SDK client, HTTP/WebSocket transports and examples; root imports expose Client/AsyncClient/chat. _sdk_session.py centralizes a random UUID header shared by old and new SDK transports, rather than collecting secrets. SDK API keys authenticate requests to configured service endpoints.

trait_changes: Retain the former broad text matcher as notable metadata/lang/source/syntax/command::macos-system-delete-command-reference. It records command-shaped text without claiming a deletion.
Require a parsed rm command for shell deletion, a recognized shell-execution API with a bound first argument for Python shell deletion, or rmtree with a bound first system-root argument.

Require shell=True on the same subprocess call. Nearby shell=True, shell=False, a validator named rmtree_validator, test vectors, shell comments, echo arguments, heredocs, and SDK staging paths do not establish system deletion.
Direct deletion atoms are suspicious in their own right; no test-filename or package-identity exclusion is added.
limits: Static analysis, not a full runtime audit. No machine deployment, user consent, network traffic or operator intent was supplied. Legitimate shell execution, file access, model requests and opt-out telemetry capabilities remain notable; their presence alone does not establish compromise.
dependency_resolution_context: pyproject.toml has optional self-extras (qwenpaw[local,whisper,codex,qoder], qwenpaw[sip]) and dashscope>=1.0.0 in the sip extra. These declarations are unchanged from beta.2; fetched wheels are resolved dependencies, not newly embedded source-archive payloads.

verification.sample_execution: No sample code was executed; scanners and static code/fact inspection only.
